title: Data Annotation Attributes and Client-Side Validation
description: Deep-dive into built-in data annotation attributes, building custom validation attributes, and enabling unobtrusive client-side validation in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: Data annotations are a set of attributes in the System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations namespace that let you declare validation rules directly on your model properties. Instead of writing if-statements in every controller action, you apply an attribute once and ASP.NET Core enforces it automatically during model binding — on both the server and the client.

terms.definition: An attribute from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations applied to a model property to declare a validation rule.
The base class for all data annotation validation attributes; override IsValid() to create custom rules.
A jQuery-based technique that reads HTML5 data attributes emitted by ASP.NET Core to perform client-side validation without inline JavaScript.
The core jQuery plugin that provides validation rules and error messages in the browser.
An interface a model can implement to provide cross-field validation logic that attributes alone cannot express.

data.text: ASP.NET Core ships with a rich set of built-in validation attributes. Each attribute targets a specific validation scenario and works automatically once applied to a model property.

rows: Ensures a value is provided (not null or empty).
Limits the maximum number of characters.
Sets the minimum number of characters.
Ensures a numeric value is within a range.
Ensures two properties hold the same value.
Validates a credit card number format.

data.title: RegistrationViewModel with Data Annotations
Combine attributes for layered validation
data.text: Stack multiple attributes on one property for progressive checks. [Required] ensures a value exists, [StringLength] controls size, and [RegularExpression] enforces format — all without writing a single line of controller code.

When built-in attributes don't cover your rule, inherit from ValidationAttribute and override the IsValid() method. The method receives the property value and a ValidationContext, and returns a ValidationResult indicating success or failure.

data.title: Custom Validation Attribute — FutureDateValidator
Applying the Custom Attribute on the Model

data.text: The controller no longer needs manual DOB checks — the [FutureDateValidator] attribute handles it on both server and (partially) client side.

For validation rules that involve two or more properties (e.g., EndDate must be after StartDate), implement the IValidatableObject interface on your model. The Validate() method receives the full model, so you can compare any properties.

data.title: Cross-Field Validation Using IValidatableObject

data.text: Client-side validation gives users instant feedback in the browser without a server round-trip. ASP.NET Core uses jQuery Validation and jQuery Unobtrusive Validation to achieve this. ASP.NET Core automatically emits HTML5 data-val-* attributes on form controls when data annotations are present.

data.title: Steps to enable client-side validation
items: Add the jQuery, jQuery Validation, and jQuery Unobtrusive Validation scripts to your project (via LibMan, npm, or CDN).
Add the validation scripts to your layout or view (usually in the Scripts section).
Ensure the <form> tag has asp-action and method attributes.
Use asp-for, asp-validation-for, and asp-validation-summary tag helpers in your form.

data.title: Enabling Validation Scripts in _Layout.cshtml
data.code:
<!-- Add before closing </body> tag in _Layout.cshtml -->
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.6.0.min.js"></script>
<script src="~/lib/jquery-validation/dist/jquery.validate.min.js"></script>
<script src="~/lib/jquery-validation-unobtrusive/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js"></script>
@await RenderSectionAsync("Scripts", required: false)

data.title: Client-side validation is not a security boundary
data.text: Users can disable JavaScript or bypass client-side checks entirely. Always keep server-side data annotation validation — it is the authoritative enforcement. Client-side validation only improves the user experience.

Remote validation checks a value against the server via an AJAX call — typically triggered when the user tabs out of a field. It is ideal for checking uniqueness (e.g., is the username already taken?) without submitting the entire form.

data.title: Remote Validation Action — Check Username Availability
Applying [Remote] on the Username Property

data.text: When the user tabs out of the Username field, jQuery Unobtrusive sends an AJAX GET request to /Account/CheckUsername?username=value. The server returns true (valid) or an error string (invalid). The error is displayed next to the field automatically.

data.text: Exercise: Build a Validated Registration Form

data.title: End-to-End Validated Registration Form
data.description: Create a complete registration form demonstrating data annotations, client-side validation, custom validation attributes, and remote validation.
steps: Create RegistrationViewModel with FullName, Username, Email, Password, ConfirmPassword, and Age properties — each with at least two data annotation attributes.
Create a custom [NoSpecialChars] attribute that rejects usernames containing spaces or special characters.
Apply the custom attribute to the Username property.
Create the AccountController with a CheckUsername action for remote validation.
Build the Razor form with asp-validation-summary and asp-validation-for on each field.
Submit with invalid data and confirm errors appear instantly in the browser without a server request.
data.expectedOutcome: Invalid submissions show client-side errors immediately. The [Remote] check fires asynchronously on username blur. A fully valid form passes ModelState.IsValid on the server.

items.question: Do data annotations work in API controllers?
items.answer: Yes. When a controller has [ApiController], ASP.NET Core automatically returns a 400 Bad Request with a ValidationProblemDetails response if ModelState is invalid, without you needing to check ModelState.IsValid manually.

items.question: Can I use data annotations with Razor Pages?
items.answer: Absolutely. Razor Pages use the same model binding and validation pipeline as MVC controllers. Apply [BindProperty] on the PageModel property and all data annotations work identically.

items.question: How do I localize validation error messages?
items.answer: Use resource files (.resx) and the ErrorMessageResourceType and ErrorMessageResourceName properties on any validation attribute: [Required(ErrorMessageResourceType = typeof(Resources), ErrorMessageResourceName = "NameRequired")]

items.question: Can a custom attribute access the database during validation?
items.answer: Not directly — ValidationAttribute.IsValid() has no DI context. Use IValidatableObject.Validate() for DI access, or perform database checks in the controller using ModelState.AddModelError() or a remote validation action.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Data annotations declare validation rules as attributes on model properties — no controller code needed.
Built-in attributes cover most scenarios: Required, StringLength, Range, RegularExpression, Compare, EmailAddress, Phone, Url.
Custom validation attributes inherit from ValidationAttribute and override IsValid() for reusable business rules.
IValidatableObject.Validate() handles cross-field validation that attributes alone cannot express.
Client-side validation uses jQuery Validation + Unobtrusive Validation for instant browser feedback.
ASP.NET Core emits data-val-* HTML attributes automatically from data annotations.
Remote validation ([Remote] attribute) performs server-side checks via AJAX when a field loses focus.
Client-side validation improves UX but server-side validation is always the authoritative check.
data.takeaway: Mastering data annotations and client-side validation lets you enforce data integrity with minimal code while delivering a responsive user experience.
